content.text: No exclusivity obligation binding Corio appears anywhere: the licence grants are non-exclusive in Vendor's favour, Exhibit D cooperation is expressly non-binding, and there is no sourcing, requirements, or non-compete covenant on Corio.

input.quote: The parties agree to the following non-binding sales and marketing cooperation efforts:
input.rationale: The Agreement imposes no exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation on Corio, so it meets the preferred position. The Section 2 grants run in the other direction (each licence to Corio is "nonexclusive"), Section 2.4 gives Corio a distribution right without any requirements commitment, and Section 14.8 confirms Corio "shall solely direct the provision of Corio Services and may subcontract certain portions of the Corio Services to third parties". Exhibit D's sales and marketing cooperation (including cross-selling incentives, joint marketing and the two-initial-customer effort) is expressly "non-binding" cooperation, not an exclusive-ASP or exclusive-sourcing covenant, and nothing restricts Corio from licensing or hosting competing procurement software. The only exclusivity-flavoured protections here (Commerce One not contacting Corio Customers for non-ASP licence sales and referring them to Corio) benefit Corio and are not flagged. No redline required.
